correctness.rationale: Schur orthogonality on standard S_n matrix coefficients gives sample Gram ((n−1)/n!)(2I+B^TB+(n−5)J). The three products of edge-transpositions give exactly n−1, n−4, n−5. Complete K_n incidence BB^T=(n−2)I+J yields positive eigenlevels n(n−3)^2/2, n and 2 for n≥4; arbitrary edge masks are positive-definite principal submatrices. Unsigned-incidence kernel has dimension m−n+b; for r-regular graphs BB^T=rI+A gives all spectral levels and exact condition number at n≥6,r≥3. Complete-class restriction kernel consists exactly of skew-symmetric coefficient matrices.
risks: The universal proof relies on orthogonality and exact incidence identities, not on these three finite n checks.
